name: fix_flask_unique_constraint
description: Enforces unique email across a repository check and a 409 in the blueprint
prompts: Registration must reject duplicate emails, but both layers are broken: UserRepository.email_exists in app/repository.py always returns False, and the POST /users handler in app/routes/users.py never checks it. Fix BOTH: make email_exists correctly report whether an email is already registered, and have the handler return HTTP 409 with JSON {"error": ...} when the email is taken - BEFORE adding, so a rejected duplicate creates nothing (does not consume an id). A first registration returns 201; a duplicate returns 409; a different email returns 201 with the next id.

setup_files.app/__init__.py:
from flask import Flask

from app.routes.users import users_bp


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.register_blueprint(users_bp)
    return app

test_setup_files.test_unique.py:
from app import create_app

client = create_app().test_client()

r = client.post("/users", json={"email": "a@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 201 and r.get_json()["id"] == 1, r.data

r = client.post("/users", json={"email": "a@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 409, f"duplicate must be 409, got {r.status_code}"

r = client.post("/users", json={"email": "b@x.io"})
assert r.status_code == 201, r.data
assert r.get_json()["id"] == 2, f"rejected duplicate consumed an id: {r.get_json()}"
print("PASS")
